rules.statement: Don't read a hierarchy with unbounded fan-out (every descendant of a node) as one list; walk it depth first, reading one bounded page of children per level, so memory is bounded by depth times page size.
rules.why: A node can have any number of children, so reading a whole subtree as one list grows without bound in memory and result size. A breadth-first walk has the same problem because one level can be arbitrarily wide.
rules.check: Look for store methods or queries that return all descendants of a tree node at once, or breadth-first walks that hold a whole level in memory, where a paged child read with a depth-first walk would work.

rules.statement: Don't use keyset (seek) pagination over a string column whose sort order depends on the database collation; page by a key whose ordering the database guarantees to be stable.
rules.why: A collation-dependent order can make a page boundary skip or repeat a row.
rules.check: Look for paged queries that order by and filter `> lastValue` on a text column such as a path or name, and check whether the comparison and the ordering could disagree under the database collation.

rules.statement: When a paged walk reads from a store, run each page read as its own untracked query in its own short unit of work, and don't hold one context or transaction open for the whole walk.
rules.why: Holding at most one page per level, each read in its own unit of work, keeps the walk's memory and tracked-entity state bounded no matter how large the tree is.
rules.check: Look for EF Core walks or loops that reuse one tracked DbContext across all pages, or that leave out `AsNoTracking` on read-only page queries.
